message.content: In domestic cats and many other mammals, the presence of a mane (or “mane‑like” hair growth) is typically governed by a dominant allele. In lions, the same principle applies: the gene that causes the characteristic thick, dark mane in adult male lions is dominant over the allele that would produce a non‑mane phenotype. Thus, if a lion inherits one copy of the dominant mane allele from either parent, it will develop the full, dark mane seen in mature male lions.
